source_snapshot.test_set: Intel CPU RAS -DRAM Parity Persistent Error
source_snapshot.procedure: Enable listed EDKII debug/WHEA controls, deploy Intel ITP, boot Windows, log and halt, run mc.dimminfo(), require CAP on, then issue literal `ei.injectCMDParityPersistent(socket, hbm=-1, mc, channel)` and resume.
source_snapshot.criteria: OS dmesg reports the matching error; BMC records a DIMM uncorrectable error without slot information; the front-panel fault light turns on; DIMM lightpath may turn on; optional UEFI records a DIMM uncorrectable error; Cscript reports successful CMD parity injection.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; delegates persistent parity injection to the user/FAE and proposes parity/persistent/uncorrected dmesg plus BMC SEL capture.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CHANGED; adds CAP/target validation, persistent-state clear/recovery, bounded injection, indicators and restoration.
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 1. Bios Setting EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> Lock Chipset -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> MSR Lock Control -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> EV DFX features -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> Disable BIOS Done -> [‘X’] EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> WHEA Error Injection Support -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> Whea PCIE Error Injection Action Table -> Enabled 2. Deploy Intel ITP environment. 3. Boot SUT into Windows. 4. Execute Intel Cscripts on the client 5. Using the following command >>>itp.log("C:\Test.log") >>>halt() >>>mc.dimminfo() 6. Check 'CAP' parameter in dimminfo is 'on'. >>>ei.injectCMDParityPersistent(socket, hbm=-1, mc, channel) >>>go 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. Check OS dmesg reports the error that match 2. BMC error log should record DIMM uncorrectable error but no slot info 3. Front Panel fault Light will Light if there is one 4. DIMM lightpath may light 5. uEFI SEL Log should record DIMM uncorrectable error if there is one 6. Cscript should show CMD Parity Error Injection is successful.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- Memory controller 1~N (Intel persistent DRAM parity on Memory controller 1~N error injection): requires CScripts/EDKII unlock (Lock Chipset=Disable, MSR Lock Control=Disable, EV DFX Features=Enable, WHEA Error Injection Support=Enable) + the user/FAE to drive the Cscript/error-injection harness for this exact pattern. Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'parity|persistent|uncorrected'; echo __persistent_DRAM_parity_on_Memory_controller_1~N; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".

disposition_reason: A persistent command/address parity error is not merely a higher-severity transient event: it can recur after resume and prevent normal boot until a vendor-specific state is cleared. The source command is syntactically invalid, so the precise package interface must be supplied rather than inferred. Evidence must demonstrate both that the intended controller produced the persistent UCE and that the approved clear/recovery operation returned the platform to a clean state. Because those inputs are obtainable from the FAE and the intent is otherwise clear, REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION remains appropriate instead of BLOCKED. test_case.test_name: Memory controller 1~N — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Inject a persistent DRAM command/address parity fault into each approved memory-controller target with CAP enabled, verify uncorrectable persistent handling and Cscript success across OS/BMC/UEFI and physical indicators, then safely clear the state and recover the platform.
required_package: Socket/controller/channel/DIMM mapping and controller 1~N coverage matrix
Approved Intel ITP/CScripts build/hash, namespace and valid injectCMDParityPersistent signature
CAP semantics plus persistence lifetime and exact clear mechanism
Dedicated-SUT approval, backup, timeout, console recovery and BIOS restoration plan
test_case.test_command: A qualified FAE/operator enables the approved debug/CAP settings, maps one socket/controller/channel target, supplies a vendor-valid persistent-parity call, performs one bounded injection, captures persistent status and uncorrectable evidence, observes fault indicators, executes the approved persistence-clear/recovery flow and restores configuration.
test_case.expected_result: 1. Check OS dmesg reports the error that match 2. BMC error log should record DIMM uncorrectable error but no slot info 3. Front Panel fault Light will Light if there is one 4. DIMM lightpath may light 5. uEFI SEL Log should record DIMM uncorrectable error if there is one 6. Cscript should show CMD Parity Error Injection is successful.

safety_gate: Dedicated idle SUT with backup, stable power, independent console and qualified FAE
Preserve pre-state and existing logs; capture exact target and persistence-clear readiness before injection
Use only the approved syntactically valid persistent command and one target at a time
Stop on wrong target/severity, error storm, data-integrity concern, no-boot or inability to clear the persistent state
No automatic retry, reset or clearing; complete recovery and configuration restoration under the runbook
expected_evidence: Owner approval and full SUT/controller/DIMM/firmware/OS/BMC identity
Package version/hash, target coverage, BIOS/CAP pre/post state and armed recovery/clear path
Exact valid persistent command and complete Cscript success/output
Time-correlated Windows/WHEA persistent UCE, BMC uncorrectable no-slot event, applicable UEFI, front-panel-on and DIMM-lightpath evidence
Crash/recovery timing, persistence-clear transcript, clean health/restoration diff and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: The persistent-state clear method is as critical as the injection itself. Its absence blocks execution but is not permission to downgrade the row to a transient test or claim DUT failure.

source_conflict.reason: The literal persistent call is non-runnable because positional `mc, channel` follow keyword `hbm=-1`; controller 1~N lacks target coverage; Windows conflicts with dmesg; the Criteria says generic Cscript CMD parity rather than persistent success; and UEFI/DIMM-lightpath applicability plus persistence clearing are undefined.
